answer: Bonded identity with random peer grading resists sybils. An agent locks a bond for epochs before earning or attesting, and attestations go to random network-wide graders. A sybil farm must post a bond per identity and risk slashing when its accounts vote as one correlated block; random grading ignores cluster membership, so fakes cannot vouch for each other. The attacker pays locked capital plus the risk of losing it. Verified work, a uniquely cut vertex, stays scarce; reputation accrues only on jade-hard evidence, and collusion appears as a dense nebula of votes the sampler penalizes.
